en.title: Tantrums at Ages Two and Three: Understanding and Prevention
en.description: Six daily lessons for a parent with a child aged two or three: understanding tantrums, noticing hunger, tiredness and transitions, safety with few words during a tantrum, closeness and naming feelings after the child calms down, understanding the repeated «no» with a few clear limits, and offering two acceptable choices instead of one order, with a calm response that keeps the child safe and meets the child's needs.

paths.band_notes: Ages 2-3: self-regulation and communication are developing. No deterministic diagnosis, guaranteed prevention, punishment, hitting or shaming. Safety, hunger, pain and distress must always be addressed. This recovery publishes only the first six contiguous lessons; the remaining original drafts (s07-s10) stay held in the preserved backup. The unit d7a09c7e-769c-48b5-aaf8-0511fedfc0db is not used (no source URL; invented quarter-hour and five-a-day thresholds). Units 179d90e1-a863-42e1-8fea-e8560b7401f7 (no source URL; 'suppression postpones the confrontation to adolescence' and a six-month threshold) and seed-defiance-23 (no exact source mapping; a non-verbatim prophetic saying) are not used by lessons 5 and 6. Lesson 3 (during the tantrum) follows AAP HealthyChildren (do not ignore hitting, kicking, biting or throwing; stop it immediately; hold a child rushing into danger; no spanking, yelling or shaming; parent's own time-out with the child in a safe place), AACAP (tired, hungry, pain or mild illness; remain calm, you are modeling; state calmly which behavior must stop; never respond with physical aggression; seek help for danger, self-harm on purpose, not able to calm down, very frequent or longer than expected for age, getting in the way of life), CDC (ensure safety first; remain close, hands free, time and space to calm; ignoring only for minor, safe, attention-seeking behavior such as whining, never needs-based, distress or danger, child not left alone unless safe, attention returned when it stops; giving in rewards the tantrum; a pause or another trusted caregiver for the parent; lost skills -> talk with the doctor) and NHS (losing your temper or shouting back will not end it; do not change your mind or bribe with sweets; distraction; holding a child who is more upset than angry, when you are calm). No duration or count threshold is given. Lesson 4 (after the tantrum): CDC emotion coaching (wait until both are calm; pause and breathe; connect with eye contact, a smile or gentle touch; name the emotion in simple words, 'it seems like you are upset' when unsure, accept the child's correction and expand; validate feelings but limit behavior, then simple choices; rushing to solutions can dismiss feelings and escalate; teach acceptable ways to show upset; return to being positive and praise), NHS (do not hit back; make clear that hitting hurts and you will not allow it; 'I know you're feeling angry' helps a child name feelings; praise and cuddles), AAP (hug and start over; no shaming; consult the pediatrician if very withdrawn, persistently sad or highly demanding most of the time). No withdrawal of love, no grudges; referral and urgent-help sentence as in lesson 3. Lesson 5 (the repeated 'no'): CDC (the 'terrible twos' as toddlers begin to assert their independence; developing independence can look like pushing away, parents may feel frustrated or rejected, this is normal, pause; adjust expectations; routines and rules with consistency, predictability and follow-through; positive elements such as a bath toy or bubbles for a resisted routine; specific labeled praise), AAP HealthyChildren (two-year-olds test limits; consistently set reasonable limits that allow exploring, draw the line at dangerous or antisocial behavior; choose your battles and accommodate when you can, consistency is key; directed choices rather than yes/no questions; praise when they dress or feed themselves; no spanking, yelling or shaming; consult the pediatrician if very passive or withdrawn, persistently sad, or highly demanding and unsatisfied most of the time) and NHS (difficult behaviour often from tiredness, hunger, frustration or boredom; consistency, everyone close to the child responds the same way; explain why, e.g. holding hands to cross the road; specific praise; a reward before the behaviour is a bribe; smacking teaches hitting is OK) and AACAP (tired, hungry, pain or mild illness; remain calm; seek help for danger, self-harm, not calming, very frequent or longer than expected, getting in the way of life). Neither 'no' nor stubbornness is called a diagnosis; no breaking the will, no claim of later confrontation, no month or count threshold. Lesson 6 (two choices): AAP (give control over little things with small directed choices rather than yes/no questions; choices among acceptable alternatives with sensible limits; prepare children for upcoming activities), CDC (simple choices such as carrots or an apple; car seat buckled every ride, so safety is not offered as a choice; predictability and follow-through, do what you say; explain changes calmly; labeled praise) and NHS (consistency; no bribes). Choices are a help, not a guarantee; if they choose neither, check needs first, then the parent calmly decides and follows through without a long negotiation, shouting or threats.

lessons.title: لماذا يغضب بهذه القوة؟
lessons.focus: Understand common toddler frustration while assessing needs and safety; calm support without labels or guarantees.

lessons.title: قبل النوبة: الجوع والنعاس والانتقال المفاجئ
lessons.focus: Notice hunger, tiredness and difficult transitions; predictable feeding/sleep routines and simple choices, without guaranteed prevention or fixed countdowns.

lessons.title: أثناء النوبة: أمانٌ وكلماتٌ قليلة
lessons.focus: During a tantrum: safety first (move harmful things away; stop hitting, biting, kicking, throwing or self-harm at once, calmly and without violence; hold a child rushing into danger); check tiredness, hunger, pain or illness and meet the need; stay close, give time to calm, few calm words; do not shout, hit, threaten or humiliate; a gentle hug if more sad than angry; do not give in or bribe after a reasoned no; turn attention away only from minor safe attention-seeking behaviour such as whining, while watching, never from need, pain, illness, fear or distress; parent's own pause with the child safe or with a trusted adult; referral and urgent help without numeric thresholds.

lessons.title: بعد أن يهدأ: الحضن أولًا ثم الكلمات
lessons.focus: After the tantrum: both calm first; closeness before words (hug if the child wants it, gentle touch, eye contact and a smile); name the feeling simply, accept correction; validate the feeling and limit the behaviour without a lecture, offer two simple choices; teach an acceptable way to say they are upset; do not rush to solutions; if they hit, say clearly that hitting hurts and is not allowed, never hit back; no shaming, return to the day warmly and praise words over screaming; referral (very frequent, longer than expected, cannot calm, harm, lost skills, persistently sad or withdrawn) and urgent help.

lessons.title: «لا» الصغيرة: العناد علامة نموّ
lessons.focus: The repeated 'no' at two and three: part of growing independence and testing limits, not a verdict on child or parent; check tiredness, hunger, frustration or boredom first; a few clear, consistent limits for safety and harm, explained simply, flexible on small matters; say what will happen as a calm statement instead of a yes/no question when 'no' is not an option; make a resisted routine more fun; everyone responds the same way and follows through; specific praise for cooperation; never hit, shout, threaten or shame; the parent's own pause; referral and urgent help without numeric thresholds.

lessons.title: خياران بدل أمرٍ واحد
lessons.focus: Offering two choices that are both acceptable to the parent instead of a yes/no question or a bare order (control over little things); no choice where safety is concerned, such as the car seat: state it calmly and do it; tell them beforehand what will happen next; if they choose neither, check needs, then the parent decides calmly and follows through without long negotiation; specific praise; choices help but do not guarantee cooperation; no bribes, shouting or threats.
